title: Menuella Footnote Codes
description: The short code printed next to a disclosure in a menu legend, mapped from the semantic key. One scheme, valid in any region. The allergen letters (A1–R) follow long-established EU menu practice so guests recognise them; the declaration numbers are Menuella's own contiguous 1–22, because national legends are not standardized and the same number means different things on different menus. A code is a RENDERING convention, never an identity: store the key, render the code, and when reading someone else's menu resolve it against that menu's own legend first.

scheme.description: Identifies the numbering scheme, so a consumer can tell these codes apart from a national legend it may also handle.

convention.description: Plain-English note on what the numbering is and the limits of trusting it.

allergens.description: Allergen key from data/allergens.json → printed code.

declarations.description: Declaration key from data/declarations.json → printed code.

additionalProperties.description: The printed footnote code, as a string — a letter (A6, G) or a number (11). A string rather than a number so both kinds share one type.
